articles.summary: Light carries information in both amplitude and phase, although cameras record only intensity. Reconstructing the optical field is at the heart of wavefront sensing, microscopy and coherent communications. Existing methods often rely on multiple measurements or iterative phase retrieval. In fields described by known spatial modes, intensity is determined by pairwise products of their complex coefficients. Yet optical symmetries can make these products indistinguishable, leaving different fields with nearly identical images. Here, we show that engineering the optical measurement to break these symmetries enables direct reconstruction of the complex field from a single intensity image. …

articles.title: Multifunctional Electromagnetic Control in Cascaded Metasurfaces Enabled by Directional‐Rotational Configurations
articles.authors: Zhicai Yu, Bowen Zou, Haojun Jiang, Yi Li, Sicheng Yan, Long Chen, Jian Lin Su, Zi Xuan Cai, Zhou He, Xinyu Li, Jian Wei You
institutions: State Key Laboratory of Millimeter Waves
articles.summary: Metasurfaces offer versatile platforms for multifunctional electromagnetic‐wave manipulation, yet extending the number and diversity of accessible functions remains challenging because conventional multiplexing schemes rely on independently addressable physical degrees of freedom. Here, we demonstrate a directional‐rotational cascaded (DRC) metasurface in which the electromagnetic response is jointly controlled by propagation direction, relative in‐plane rotation, and incident‐field condition. A single fabricated two‐layer device experimentally realizes ten heterogeneous functions spanning electromagnetic computing, holography, focusing, and vortex‐beam generation. …

articles.summary: As a promising 3D display technology, holographic display can reconstruct full light field information of 3D scenes, including depth cues. While depth‐dependent defocus naturally provides these depth cues, the limited depth of focus (DOF) restricts the axial range of image clarity, posing a significant challenge for layer‐based holographic displays. In this work, we innovatively propose a large‐DOF and high‐quality layer‐based holographic 3D display system based on a liquid crystal axicon. The core components of the proposed system include a spatial light modulator (SLM) loaded with high‐quality holograms and a specially designed liquid crystal axicon. …

articles.summary: Spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) generates correlated photon pairs that inherently exhibit high-dimensional spatial entanglement in orbital angular momentum (OAM) modes. In practice, the resulting two-photon states are typically not maximally entangled due to a highly non-uniform distribution of generated OAM modes. Although pump-beam engineering has emerged as a tool to prepare high-dimensional entangled states, it has usually been restricted to low-dimensional subspaces, i.e., small sets of selected OAM modes for each photon within the full infinite-dimensional two-photon Hilbert space. …

articles.authors: Anzhou Wen, Hengyu Lian, Kevin Wu, Maxwell F. Parsons, Praneeth Chakravarthula
articles.summary: Optical tweezers use tightly focused laser beams to trap and manipulate individual particles, enabling advances in quantum computing, drug discovery, and biological research. Scaling these technologies to large arrays requires delivering sufficient light to every trapping site while minimizing the total laser power required. Here, we investigate the fundamental limits of how efficiently a phase-only hologram can distribute light across an array of optical traps. We derive upper bounds on the minimum intensity across trapping sites, accounting for illumination, target geometry, and diffraction from spatial light modulator pixels. …

We show that the astigmatism observed in the semimonolithic configuration can be fully compensated by introducing a third mirror to fold the cavity, thereby exploiting the geometric astigmatism arising from oblique incidence on the curved mirror. …

articles.summary: We study OAM transfer in backward wave parametric oscillators pumped by vortex beams. While total OAM is preserved, nonlinear gain favors the strongest spatial overlap, leading to dominant mode selection absent in the low-gain regime.

institutions: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique
articles.summary: We demonstrate a multimode GRIN Er/Yb fiber laser generating ~2-ps mode-locked pulses with over 20-nJ energy and ~10-kW peak power. Nonlinear intermodal interactions enable spatiotemporal mode-locking, while the GRIN profile produces near-Gaussian output via beam self-cleaning — the first such demonstration in an all-anomalous dispersion regime.

articles.summary: We propose a configuration-controlled optical encryption framework using multimode fibers (MMF), where distinct fiber configurations encode images into complex speckle patterns. A reconfigurable diffractive neural network (Re-DNN) selectively decrypts multiple datasets through configuration-dependent operations without retraining.

articles.summary: Janus metasurfaces possess an unparalleled capacity to asymmetrically tailor electromagnetic wavefronts for forward and backward propagation paths, opening new avenues for practical implementation in asymmetric information processing. Here, we propose a strategy for simultaneous phase and polarization modulation of incident terahertz (THz) waves leveraging a cascaded metasurface architecture (i.e., Janus metalens). …

articles.summary: Optical focusing is a fundamental tool for tailoring structured light, yet efforts to actively control vortex dynamics have largely been concentrated in the tight-focusing regime. Here we demonstrate tunable propagation dynamics of an optical vortex dipole under paraxial focusing, where the thin-lens quadratic phase and the initial intervortex distance act as two control knobs. Their interplay regulates the intrinsic vortex–antivortex interaction, which steers the dipole into an OAM Hall effect in real space. The same critical vortex position also governs the emergence of a spectral vortex dipole in Fourier space. …

articles.summary: Optical manipulation provides a powerful means of controlling microscopic particles, and optical pulling is particularly attractive because it enables particle transport against the incident momentum. Here, we establish a finite-multipole accessibility framework that provides a formal upper-bound criterion for determining whether optical pulling is excluded or kinematically permitted within a truncated multipolar space. …

articles.authors: Yaru Gao, Chuanyao Geng, Pujuan Ma, Xin Liu, Chunhao Liang, Yangjian Cai, Qian Chen
articles.summary: Spiral–pinhole arrays offer a simple binary approach to optical vortex generation, especially in spectral regions lacking programmable phase modulators, but conventional designs mainly produce annular beams with limited geometric control. Here, we propose geometric pinhole encoding for flexible synthesis of polygonal vortex beams. A prescribed polygonal contour is mapped onto a nonuniform azimuthal phase with a total circulation of 2 π l , where l is the topological charge, and then encoded into the radial coordinates of discrete pinholes through propagation-induced optical path differences. …

articles.authors: Faorlin T, Panzl L, Grosser P, Viñas P, Kahan A, Hörmann WJ, Weiser Y, Cerchiari G, Feldker T, Erhard A, Jacob G, Ulmanis J, Blatt R, Bermudez A, Monz T
articles.summary: Spectral crowding of collective motional modes limits the fidelity of entangling interactions in trapped-ion quantum processors by inducing off-resonant coupling to spectator modes. We introduce a geometric-phase entangling interaction driven by a transverse, time-dependent structured-light force. By applying the force in a plane orthogonal to the optical propagation direction, we reduce the effects of spectral crowding while preserving single-ion addressing. The scheme is compatible with arbitrary qubit encodings, provided that the qubit states experience a differential AC Stark shift. …
